newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia arrests Bosnian Croat warlord from Mostar.
newsitem.headline: Croatia arrests Bosnian Croat warlord from Mostar.

text.p: Croatian police have arrested a Bosnian Croat warlord, often accused by international mediators of having connections with organised crime in the divided town of Mostar, the Croatian news agency Hina said on Wednesday.
Mladen Naletilic, also known as Tuta, was arrested on Monday in the Split region of southern Croatia and brought to Zagreb for questioning, the agency quoted the Interior Ministry as saying.
Naletilic was arrested "on a well-founded suspicion that he was involved in committing a criminal act liable to official prosecution", the police told Hina without specifying the nature of the act.
No official comment or confirmation was available.

The arrest coincided with Western pressure on the Croatian government to bring into line ethnic Croats who oppose building joint political institutions with their nominal Moslem allies in the Bosnian Federation.

International police investigators reported on Tuesday that Bosnian Croat police fired on unarmed Moslems without cause and behaved in a criminal manner in an incident earlier this month in which a Moslem civilian was killed in Mostar.
A diplomat in Sarajevo, who asked not to be named, said another prominent warlord in western Croat-held Mostar, Vinko Martinovic, known as "Stela", had escaped arrest.

"Croat police tried to arrest him but he escaped and he is on the run. A warrant has been issued for his arrest," the source told Reuters. It was not clear when or where Croat police had attempted to nab Martinovic.

Naletilic has frequently been accused by Western mediators of being at the centre of a powerful mafia cartel that runs the western part of Mostar and opposes international efforts to build a stable peace in the region.
During the Bosnian war he commanded a notorious paramilitary unit of the Bosnian Croat HVO militia which operated in the Mostar area.
Paramilitary units connected with mafia are held largely responsible for lawlessness in the western half of the sharply divided town, especially for the continuous evictions of Moslem inhabitants.
